newsitem.title: USA: Armco sees higher fabricated products profit.
newsitem.headline: Armco sees higher fabricated products profit.

text.p: Specialty steelmaker Armco Inc said Wednesday it expected operating profit to improve for its Fabricated Products segment in the second quarter.
Armco said Douglas Dynamics, the segment's snowplow and ice control products manufacturer, was moving into the preseason sales period for its primary products.
Sawhill Tubular was also expected to remain slightly profitable in a very competitive market, it added.
The Fabricated Products segment had an operating profit of $2.6 million on sales of $66.3 million for the first quarter, compared to $1.5 million on sales of $58.3 million a year ago.
Armco had first-quarter earnings of $0.05 a share against $0.02 for the same period a year ago. Sales totaled $441.3 million against $430.4 million.
"Despite lower prices across most of our product lines, Armco's operating profit represented a marked improvement compared to the first quarter of 1996," it said.
Operating profit totalled $19.2 million for the first quarter against $15.1 million.
"Demand for automotive exhaust stainless steels and electrical steels was strong, but imports continued to have a significant negative impact on volume and pricing," it said.
Armco said the outlook for the second quarter was nevertheless positive as orders for automotive exhaust stainless and electrical steels continued to be strong.
It said it expected a limited benefit in the second quarter from price increases, effective May 5.
Armco makes specialty flat-rolled stainless, electrical and galvanized steels. It also makes snowplows and ice control products and standard pipe and tubular products.
